---
title: "Development and installation"
---

Run commands from the checkout containing Cargo.toml, crates/, and examples/.
Polyscope workspaces are separate checkouts from the original project directory.
Source changes and build outputs in a workspace do not automatically appear in
another checkout. The gitignored target/ directory must be rebuilt there after
transferring source changes.

## Environment


Following the official [ext-php-rs installation guide](https://ext-php.rs/getting-started/installation.html)
and [Hello World build workflow](https://ext-php.rs/getting-started/hello_world.html):

```sh
# macOS: Xcode command-line tools, Rust, PHP (includes headers), libclang
xcode-select --install
brew install rust php llvm
export PHP="$(brew --prefix php)/bin/php"
export PHP_CONFIG="$(brew --prefix php)/bin/php-config"
export PATH="$(brew --prefix php)/bin:$PATH"
# If bindgen cannot find libclang:
export LIBCLANG_PATH="$(brew --prefix llvm)/lib"
```

Linux (Debian/Ubuntu with PHP 8.3+ available in the configured repositories):

```sh
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install build-essential clang libclang-dev php-cli php-dev curl
# Install stable Rust using https://rustup.rs, then source ~/.cargo/env.
export PHP="$(command -v php)"
export PHP_CONFIG="$(command -v php-config)"
```

Check `php -v`, `php-config --version`, and `rustc --version`. PHP and php-config
must belong to the same installation (including architecture, ZTS/NTS and debug
mode). `scripts/check` and `scripts/check-fpm` take PHP from `php-config
--php-binary` unless `PHP` is set, so a different `php` earlier on PATH, such as
Herd's, does not matter to them. Commands you run by hand still need the
matching `php`.
The macOS linker configuration permits symbols resolved by PHP when it loads the
extension; Linux needs no macOS linker flags.

When using Homebrew LLVM's libclang on macOS, select the matching compiler and
builtin header directory as well. Mixing Xcode's older arm_neon.h with a newer
libclang can fail before any statistical tests run:

```sh
export LIBCLANG_PATH="$(brew --prefix llvm)/lib"
export CC="$(brew --prefix llvm)/bin/clang"
export CXX="$(brew --prefix llvm)/bin/clang++"
export BINDGEN_EXTRA_CLANG_ARGS="-resource-dir=$($CC -print-resource-dir) -isysroot=$(xcrun --show-sdk-path)"
```

The CI matrix disables fail-fast so a macOS failure does not cancel Linux evidence.

## Build and run

Run from the repository root with the environment above:

```sh
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo build -p phit --locked
# macOS:
export STATS_EXTENSION="$PWD/target/debug/libphit.dylib"
# Linux instead:
# export STATS_EXTENSION="$PWD/target/debug/libphit.so"
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" -m
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" -r 'echo Phit\hello(), PHP_EOL;'
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" tests/ols.php
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" tests/logistic.php
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" tests/probit.php
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" tests/poisson.php
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" tests/lmm.php
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" tests/r-compatibility.php
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" tests/lmm-expanded.php
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" tests/logistic-mixed.php
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" examples/ols.php
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" examples/logistic.php
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" examples/probit.php
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" examples/poisson.php
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" examples/lmm.php
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" examples/lmm-slopes.php
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" examples/logistic-mixed.php
```

For persistent installation, the official optional [cargo-php workflow](https://ext-php.rs/getting-started/cargo-php.html)
is `cargo install cargo-php --locked`, then from `crates/php-extension`,
`cargo php install --release`. Back up php.ini first. Alternatively build with
`cargo build -p phit --release --locked` and add
`extension=/absolute/path/to/target/release/libphit.dylib` (Linux: `.so`)
to the CLI php.ini shown by `php --ini`. Then `php examples/ols.php` runs directly.
Rebuild for each PHP version; `-n` skips ini files for isolated development tests.

For PIE installation, container builds, production FPM checks and release artifacts,
see [installation and deployment](deployment.qmd).

## Running in an application

Build the release extension against the PHP installation used by the application.
Deploy the library for that OS, architecture, PHP version and build configuration;
a macOS dylib cannot be used by a Linux server. Keep the deployed library at a
permanent absolute path and enable it in the relevant PHP configuration.

CLI and PHP-FPM may read different ini files. Enable the extension for FPM as well
as CLI when serving web requests, and restart FPM after installation or replacement.
Verify `extension_loaded('phit')` and `function_exists('fit_ols')` and `function_exists('fit_logistic')` in the
actual application runtime. Once enabled, application code calls fit_ols(), fit_logistic(), fit_probit() or fit_poisson()
directly. There is no per-call import, autoloader or Composer dependency.

PHP loads the library when it starts. Each call synchronously converts PHP arrays
into owned Rust numeric vectors, fits the model, and returns an associative array.
It does not launch R, a subprocess, or an external service. The deployed runtime
needs the compiled library and its platform dependencies; Rust/Cargo and R are
build/development tools.

## Numerical dependency policy

The engine uses nalgebra's Rust-native SVD and QR. There is one maintained numerical
path, with no BLAS/LAPACK dependency or backend selection. We defer external
numerical backends until a concrete requirement justifies the additional build
and deployment work. The earlier Accelerate trial is retained as
[historical benchmark evidence](benchmarks/ols.qmd#apple-accelerate-experiment);
its Cargo feature and foreign-call wrapper have been removed.

The posterior-draw kernels also use nalgebra Cholesky, triangular solves and
pivoted LU. Their [numerical notes](draw-numerics.qmd) document covariance/rank
tolerances and independent fixtures; `tests/draws.php` is included in `scripts/check`.

## Changing the implementation

Keep statistical calculations in crates/stats-core and PHP conversion in
crates/php-extension. Work in small increments with established numerical crates.
Check APIs against the dependency versions in Cargo.lock. Explain important
mathematical steps near the code, and update contracts and reference tests when
behavior changes. Do not add abstractions for hypothetical models.

Follow [verification.qmd](verification.qmd) for the checks appropriate to a change.
The tested baseline is Apple Silicon, Rust 1.99 and Homebrew PHP 8.5.10. Linux container/PIE/FPM evidence is now recorded in
[deployment verification](deployment.qmd#deployment-verification); other configurations
remain subject to the supported-matrix checks.

The general mixed fitter also uses pinned Rust-native `bobyqa` and `argmin`
(Nelder–Mead). These add no C/Fortran, BLAS or LAPACK runtime requirements.
See [R compatibility](r-compatibility.qmd) for reference regeneration and the
remaining native optimizer backend work.

See the [v0.1 stabilization assessment](v0.1.qmd) for the offline `scripts/check` gate,
IDE stubs, structured diagnostics, stress fixtures, provenance manifest,
performance preservation and remaining release/deployment gates.
